title: SMART Photonics and GF launch unique photonics foundry
key_facts: SMART Photonics (Eindhoven) and GlobalFoundries announced the first open-access foundry service combining silicon photonics with indium phosphide (InP) chips.
InP supplies the active parts (lasers, amplifiers); silicon handles passive light routing; GF makes a cavity in silicon into which SMART flip-chips its lasers and amplifiers.
Targets: AI data centres (800G and 1.6T optical links), optical transceivers, LiDAR, medical equipment.
The two firms worked together for over a year on dimensional compatibility and optical coupling.
The service is expected in the second half of 2027; until then they qualify processes, design tools and packaging.
GF says the platform suits pluggable transceivers and co-packaged optics.
IO+ frames it as strengthening Europe's photonics position and the PhotonDelta programme.
quote_evidence: SMART Photonics and GlobalFoundries (GF) are introducing the first open-access foundry for integrated photonics that combines silicon and indium phosphide (InP).
The joint foundry service is expected in the second half of 2027.
why_it_matters_hint: Faster, cheaper optical links are a bottleneck for AI data centres, and this is a supply path outside Asia, though it is two years away.
notes: IO+ is a curated Dutch innovation news site; text reads as based on a joint company announcement. 'First' claim is the companies' own.
